title: Beta-multiplier bias
description: The constant-$g_m$ (beta-multiplier) self-biased reference. A top current mirror forces equal currents down two legs; the bottom devices are a diode-connected small device and a K-times-wider device with a source resistor $R_{bias}$. Because both carry the same current but the wide device runs at a lower current density, the wide device needs less gate-source voltage, and the difference is dropped across $R_{bias}$. Setting that up makes the reference's transconductance depend only on the resistor and the ratio, not on the current or the process: the square-law hand identity is $g_m = (2/R_{bias})*(1 - 1/\sqrt{K_{bm}})$. Like a Widlar, the loop is a fixed point this sheet CHECKS rather than solves: you pick the current and resistor and a requirement tests that the gate-source difference equals $I_{bias}*R_{bias}$, tuning until it closes. The $g_m$ identity is offered as a guardrail, an estimate, because it comes from the square-law model while the lookup $g_m$ is the truth; the guardrail shows how far the classic formula is off at this inversion level. The circuit has a second, zero-current stable state, so a startup subcircuit is required in practice; it is a simulation-only concern and is not sized here. The resistor-side device's source sits $I_{bias}*R_{bias}$ above ground (declared as $V_{SB}$; the demo table has no $V_{SB}$ axis, so it only warns).

params.name: I_bias
params.note: loop current in each leg; set by the resistor and ratio, so CHECK the fixed point rather than treat this as free

params.name: K_bm
params.note: width ratio of the resistor-side device to the diode device; larger K raises gm for a given resistor

params.name: R_bias
params.note: the bias resistor; sets the reference transconductance

params.name: V_dm2
params.note: drain DC level of the resistor-side device (set by the top mirror)

doc.title: Diode device (small)
doc.description: The diode-connected side of the bottom pair, carrying the loop current. Its transconductance is what the constant-gm identity pins, and its vgs is the gate rail the wide device works below.

rows.name: gm_target
rows.note: square-law constant-gm identity; an estimate the LUT gm is checked against

rows.name: delta_vgs
rows.note: the actual gate-source step from the diode device to the resistor-side device

rows.name: vgs_drop
rows.note: the gate-source step the resistor must produce for the loop to close

rules.note: the resistor-side operating point must stay within the data's weak-inversion ceiling
the constant-gm loop equation V_GS1 - V_GS2 = I_bias*R_bias, checked not solved; tune I_bias/R_bias until it closes
the classic square-law gm = (2/R)(1 - 1/sqrt(K)); the LUT gm is the truth, so this shows how far the hand formula drifts at this inversion. Estimate-grade
